album: Gentling the Horse at the Walt Whitman Mall
label: SUCK records
release_notes: First album on Rose's own label, SUCK records, following Loner, Superstar, The Art of Forgetting (New West) and the Bandcamp-only year of the slug.

Written, arranged and produced by Rose; produced, engineered and mixed by John Congleton at Animal Rites Studio, Los Angeles; additional engineering by Rachel White; mastered by Matt Colton at Metropolis Studios, London.
Rose - vocals, guitar, keys, drum machine; Zac Rae - guitar, bass, keys; Carla Azar - drums, percussion; John Congleton - drum machine.
Production connections: Congleton has also produced St. Vincent, Sharon Van Etten and Angel Olsen. Azar is the drummer of Autolux and has played on Jack White's solo albums.
Press describes a hyperreal Americana fantasy where humor, memoir and suburban dread collide, with surf-rock and spaghetti-Western touches (press coverage; Consequence).

pull_quotes.text: expansive guitar textures, touches of surf-rock, spaghetti Western flourishes

draft_comment: Out Oct. 23. Surf-flecked, spaghetti-Western indie rock with a dark sense of humor, produced by John Congleton. Calm is FCC, Goddamn Train is a caution word, and five tracks are still unscreened.

tracks.title: Yip Yip Yow
tracks.notes: Slamming guitar riff, whooping drums, upbeat and loud (WERS). Press hears psychobilly, alt-country and garage rock

tracks.title: Chow Mein
tracks.notes: Tempo sources disagree (Shazam says ~164 BPM, a critic calls it laid back). Quirky, laid-back and groovy with vocal harmonies and a polished DIY feel (If It's Too Loud). Menace and slapstick on an awkward night out (Consequence)

tracks.title: Valery (please don't be mad at me)
Conversation with Shiv (AKA liquid k song)
Hello Again, Jim
tracks.notes: Fuzz-blasted lead riff, piston-pumping drums and a surfy bassline, with a defiant, snarky vocal (Rolling Stone; See Rock Live). About toxic music-industry men named Jim (Rose, Under the Radar)

tracks.title: Calm
tracks.fcc: FCC “motherfucker” x3 (Chorus, once in each of three Choruses)
tracks.notes: Persistent distorted guitar riff, driving beat and striking percussion (She Makes Music; Teco Apple). Sarcastic, tongue-in-cheek vocal. Rose calls it a sardonic take on feeling mentally unwell (Under the Radar)

tracks.title: Everything in its Right Place
tracks.notes: Title matches Radiohead's Kid A track but it is not listed as a cover. Rose has an earlier original of the same title on year of the slug (2025); unclear whether this is a new recording
